quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks are likely still in your system three hours later?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Seven drinks minus three hours (first three hours) minus three hours (next three hours) equals one drink. But the person consumed seven drinks in the first three hours, so four drinks would remain after six hours total.

questions.question: What does smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle do?

options.text: Lets the engine help slow you down
Should only be done when no other vehicles are near

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the engine help slow you down
questions.explanation: Engine braking by downshifting helps slow your motorcycle. Use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: Why is space around your motorcycle important?

options.text: It gives you time to react to dangers
It hides you from other drivers
It stops you from avoiding dangers
It lets you look at road signs

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to dangers
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead
Change lanes and let them pass
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass you. Speeding up makes it more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle for good control?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up, not to steer
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance
Let your feet hang off the footrests
Sit far back so you have to stretch to reach the handgrips

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance in turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake
Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop quickly.

questions.question: What does a plastic face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield

questions.correctAnswerText: Your whole face
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and apply brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work. Clean the mirrors. Leave the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict happens at intersections. Stay alert and watch for vehicles that may cross in front of you.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle
The road in front of your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane beside you as possible. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is what matters most.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They will give you the right of way
It doesn't mean they see you

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't mean they see you
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver sees you. A driver may look at you and still not notice you are there.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield
It does not protect your face as well as goggles

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which of the following is NOT a hazard?
questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors hitting you, wind gusts from the vehicle, and objects thrown by passengers. These are real dangers to avoid.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly
Use it only on slippery roads
It is less effective than the rear brake
It is safe to use if you use it correctly

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe when used properly.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver guarantee?

options.text: They will give you the right of way
It does not guarantee they will give you the right of way

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will give you the right of way
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with a driver means they will give you the right of way. Do not count on it.

questions.question: What can happen if you brake too hard?

options.text: Your wheels may lose grip on the road
You will stop faster than expected
It will take too long to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels may lose grip on the road
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: What is correct when passing another vehicle?

options.text: Complete the pass without going over the speed limit
You may finish passing in a no passing zone if you started before it
You may go over the speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without going over the speed limit
questions.explanation: All passes must stay within the posted speed limit and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: In a staggered formation with several riders passing at once

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcycle riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How should you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To make a motorcycle lean and turn, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow-moving cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between cars is dangerous. You could be hit by opening car doors or cars pulling into traffic. You will not have room to move safely if a hazard appears. Also, never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What is usually safest when crossing railroad tracks that angle across your lane?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Riding straight within your lane is dangerous.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Ride on the shoulder to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad tracks while staying in your lane. Do not turn to cross at a 90-degree angle because you could move into another lane of traffic.
